entries.sense_en: in a calm, untroubled way, without being disturbed by anything around her

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; can describe staying controlled in a crisis, not only a naturally peaceful manner.
More beautiful and lofty; suggests deep, almost glowing peace.
synonyms.example: The swan glided serenely across the lake.

synonyms.nuance: Literary; stresses quiet stillness of the surroundings as well as the mood.

entries.sense_en: in a friendly, good-natured way

synonyms.nuance: Stresses easy, courteous talk; friendly and easy to approach.
synonyms.example: He chatted affably with the guests.

synonyms.nuance: Warm and cheerful; suggests a jolly, welcoming mood.
Plainer and weaker; just agreeable, without the warmth of amiably.

entries.sense_en: held in the air, ready to move but not yet moving

synonyms.nuance: Hanging without support; does not imply readiness to act.
synonyms.example: a lamp suspended from the ceiling

synonyms.nuance: Staying in the air near something, often moving slightly; less tense than poised.
synonyms.example: His finger hovered over the key.

synonyms.nuance: General word for prepared; says nothing about the physical position of a hand or body.

entries.tip_ko: ‘침착한’ 뜻도 있지만 여기서는 ‘막 움직이려고 멈춘’ 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: shouted loudly and roughly, usually in anger or complaint

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, general word for speaking very loudly.
Deep, powerful roar, like a bull; suggests a big voice and strong anger.
Short, sharp loud cry; can be excitement or pain as well as anger.

entries.sense_en: wet, muddy and half-melted, as roads are in bad winter weather

synonyms.nuance: Covered in mud; nothing to do with melted snow.
Too wet and messy; can also mean careless, so context matters.
Soaked through and soft, like wet bread or grass; not about snow.

entries.sense_en: very wet, soft ground that you sink into when you walk on it

synonyms.nuance: Larger wet area with trees and standing water; bog is soft ground, often peaty.
Flat wet land with grass and reeds; usually less deep and sticky than a bog.
A bog you can get stuck in; also used figuratively for a hopeless situation.
synonyms.example: The field turned into a quagmire.

entries.sense_en: a fast, violent flow of water

synonyms.nuance: Small, natural, usually gentle flow of water.
Water covering land that is normally dry; torrent stresses speed and force, not spread.
Overwhelming heavy rain or flood; stronger and more dramatic than torrent.

entries.sense_en: to catch sight of something passing between two other people that was not meant for you

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; does not suggest that something was meant for someone else.
Blocks a path or a message so it never arrives; more physical and final.
synonyms.example: The police cut off his escape.

synonyms.nuance: Stop someone on their way, often to talk or attack; about people, not glances.
synonyms.example: She waylaid him in the hall.

entries.sense_en: showing sympathy and sharing someone’s sadness about their bad luck

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for feeling sorry with someone, not only for a death or loss.
Share sorrow over a disappointment or bad luck; less formal than condole.
Actively comfort someone who is sad; condole is only expressing sympathy.

entries.tip_ko: ‘condole with 사람’ 형태로 쓰며, 명사 condolences(조의)가 훨씬 흔합니다.

entries.sense_en: having a large, strong, heavy body

synonyms.nuance: Short and solid; burly is big and strong overall.
Informal; heavy and muscular, sometimes a bit fat.
American for big and strong; also means hoarse-voiced.

entries.sense_en: having a healthy red face

synonyms.nuance: Common literary word for a healthy red complexion, often from outdoor life.
Temporarily red from heat, effort or emotion; rubicund is a lasting look.
Red and sometimes unhealthy-looking, as from drinking.

entries.sense_en: offered politely for someone to take

synonyms.nuance: Ordinary word for all kinds of offers; proffer is formal and used for something held out.
Formal; used for a hand, invitation or welcome.
Very formal or legal; offering something officially, such as a resignation.

entries.sense_en: brave and strong, as in old tales of heroes

synonyms.nuance: General word for not showing fear; no old-fashioned flavor.
Brave in a noble or heroic struggle, often in a losing fight.
Fearless in exploring or facing the unknown.

entries.sense_en: a very young, thin, small person

synonyms.nuance: Stresses youth and inexperience, not thinness.
synonyms.example: He was a mere boy when he left.

synonyms.nuance: Similar picture of a slight, fragile person; almost always used for girls.
synonyms.example: a wisp of a girl in a big coat

synonyms.nuance: Old-fashioned word for a thin young man not yet fully grown.

entries.tip_ko: ‘a slip of a + 명사’는 체구가 작고 어린 사람을 가리킵니다.

entries.sense_en: a holy man in India who lives by begging and is said to have magic powers
entries.sense_ko: 탁발하며 사는 인도의 수행자 (마술을 부린다고 믿음)

synonyms.nuance: Any person who gives up comforts for religious reasons; a wider, neutral term.
synonyms.example: an ascetic living in a cave

synonyms.nuance: Seeks direct spiritual experience; not necessarily poor or a beggar.
Uses magic, often evil; fakir is holy first, magical second.

entries.sense_en: at least, or to be more exact; used to correct what you just said

synonyms.nuance: Standard form; leastways is a spoken, dialect version.
synonyms.example: It’s fine, at least I think so.

synonyms.nuance: Corrects or sharpens the previous statement.
synonyms.example: He’s a doctor, or rather a nurse.

synonyms.nuance: Casually changes the point; does not correct in the same way.

entries.sense_en: in the habit of doing something; used to

synonyms.nuance: Formal; used to something, usually followed by ‘to’ plus noun or verb-ing.
Everyday way to describe a past habit; wont can also describe a general habit.
synonyms.example: He used to walk to work.

synonyms.nuance: Likely to do something because of one’s nature, not exactly habit.
synonyms.example: She is apt to forget names.

entries.modern: “is wont to regard” → “tends to look at”
entries.tip_ko: ‘won’t(…하지 않을 것이다)’와 철자가 비슷하지만 뜻이 전혀 다릅니다. 미국식으로는 보통 /wɔnt/로 발음합니다.

entries.sense_en: too bold and confident, doing things that a person of that age or rank should not

synonyms.nuance: Informal and mild; rude in a slightly amusing way.
Stronger; thinks oneself better than others, not merely overstepping.
Too eager to be familiar, especially with people one hardly knows.
synonyms.example: It was rather forward of him to ask.

entries.sense_en: a sudden, complete silence

synonyms.nuance: General word for no sound; hush suggests quiet that falls after noise, often out of awe.
A short quiet break in noise or activity, such as in a storm.
Quiet with no movement either; more peaceful and calm.

entries.sense_en: with sharp, careful attention

synonyms.nuance: With fixed, deep concentration, often in silence.
Quick and critical; can also describe a tone of voice.
Carefully and in detail; less suggestion of interest or eagerness.

entries.sense_en: in a stubborn way, refusing to change his mind

synonyms.nuance: Refusing to change, often unreasonably; the most negative of these.
Keeps going over time; neutral and not about attitude.
Positive: strong will to reach a goal.

entries.tip_ko: ‘dog(개)’처럼 물고 놓지 않는 끈기에서 온 말입니다.

entries.sense_en: an object believed to have magic power, especially to bring luck or protection

synonyms.nuance: Small lucky object, usually worn; less serious than talisman.
Worn mainly to protect against evil or illness.
Object worshipped for its spiritual power; in everyday English, often has a different meaning.

entries.sense_en: so interested that one can think of nothing else

synonyms.nuance: Very interested; can be ordinary curiosity.
Held by charm or beauty.
As if under a spell; fixed and silent, often listening to a story.

entries.sense_en: to gain a lot of profit or benefit from something

synonyms.nuance: Formal, clearly about money or advantage.
Everyday; can mean benefit of any kind, not only money.
synonyms.example: I didn’t get much out of the course.

synonyms.nuance: Informal; use an opportunity to make money, often a bit selfishly.
synonyms.example: He cashed in on his fame.

entries.tip_ko: 보통 부정문·의문문에서 ‘별 이득 없다’는 뜻으로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: of a husband: constantly nagged and controlled by his wife

synonyms.nuance: Just complained at again and again; henpecked is a whole lasting state of being ruled.
synonyms.example: He was nagged about the dishes.

synonyms.nuance: Bullied into obeying, by either sex, not only in a marriage.
Idiom: completely controlled by someone, of any relationship.

entries.tip_ko: hen(암탉)이 쪼는(peck) 모습에서 온 말로, 거의 언제나 남편에게 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a readiness to believe things without good reason
entries.sense_ko: 남의 말을 쉽게 믿어 버리는 성향

synonyms.nuance: Same idea but stronger insult: easily tricked and fooled.
synonyms.example: They took advantage of his gullibility.

synonyms.nuance: Lack of life experience; innocent, not necessarily easy to believe lies.
Positive trust with or without proof; credulity is negative.

entries.sense_en: money or profit obtained in a dishonest or unfair way

synonyms.nuance: Goods taken by theft or in war; more physical and informal.
Money from crime; everyday and blunt.
Unexpected money that comes by luck; has no idea of dishonesty.
synonyms.example: a windfall from an old aunt

entries.tip_ko: ‘ill-gotten’은 ‘나쁘게 얻은’이라는 뜻으로 gains나 wealth와 함께 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: like a monkey or ape

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday word for looking like an ape.
Plain word; often playful, not scary.
Scientific noun for the group that includes monkeys, apes and humans; not an adjective for a look.

entries.sense_en: ordinary and plain, with nothing strange or magical about it

synonyms.nuance: Dull, everyday tasks or things; slightly negative.
Boring through sameness and routine.
Positive: practical and sensible.

entries.sense_en: showed or was a sign of something

synonyms.nuance: Neutral and common; shows or points to a fact.
Formal; means or stands for something.
Literary; warns of something bad or important to come.

entries.sense_en: extremely greedy for money and wealth

synonyms.nuance: General; can be for food, money or anything.
Hoards money and hates spending it; avaricious wants to gain more.
Always trying to get more money from others, often unfairly.

entries.sense_en: fond of drinking alcohol; drinking too much

synonyms.nuance: Informal and casual; also describes things that are full of alcohol.
Describes being drunk, before a noun; bibulous describes a habit.
Plain description of someone who drinks heavily and often.

entries.tip_ko: 격식을 차리거나 익살스럽게 쓰는 어휘로, 일상에서는 드뭅니다.

entries.sense_en: nervous and uncomfortable, not relaxed

synonyms.nuance: Worried that something is wrong; can be about a situation or a feeling.
Socially clumsy or embarrassed with other people.
Broad; body or mind, mild to strong.

entries.sense_en: secretly and nervously, as if hoping not to be noticed

synonyms.nuance: Hidden from others, with no idea of fear or guilt.
Moving quietly and carefully, like a cat or thief.
Formal; doing something quietly so nobody sees, often against rules.

entries.sense_en: to begin talking about a subject that may be difficult

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for bringing up a topic; no sense of difficulty.
synonyms.example: I’ll raise it at the meeting.

synonyms.nuance: Informal, spoken version of raise.
Presents a topic or person for the first time; does not suggest awkwardness.

entries.tip_ko: ‘broach a subject’처럼 어색하거나 민감한 주제에 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: to decide something is true too quickly, before you know all the facts

synonyms.nuance: Expect the bad result without checking; narrower than jump to conclusions.
Judge a person or event fast and unfairly.
Formal, used in news and law; blames someone too quickly.

entries.sense_en: sadly, as if wishing for something he knows he cannot have

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and more eager desire; wistfully is a quiet sadness.
synonyms.example: She looked longingly at the cake.

synonyms.nuance: Plain sadness with no idea of wishing.
Sentimental about the past specifically.

entries.sense_en: stepped in and spoke, breaking into the conversation

synonyms.nuance: Stops someone talking; often rude.
Step in to change or stop a situation, not only speak.
Informal; add a comment, often helpful.
synonyms.example: She chipped in with a suggestion.

entries.sense_en: suggesting that something bad or terrible is true or will happen

synonyms.nuance: Warns that something bad will soon happen.
Threatening and openly dangerous.
Informal; frightening in a way that makes your skin crawl.

entries.sense_en: to say officially that you refuse to accept a responsibility

synonyms.nuance: Say something is not true; disclaim refuses a claim, duty or connection.
Formally give up a right or belief, often permanently.
Refuse to admit any connection, especially with a family member.

entries.sense_en: legal responsibility for something, especially for paying for damage

synonyms.nuance: General duty or blame; liability is legal and often about money.
Moral guilt for a fault, not legal duty to pay.
Duty to do something because of law, promise or morals.

entries.sense_en: quiet acceptance of a sad thing that cannot be changed

synonyms.nuance: Neutral and can be peaceful; resignation carries sadness and defeat.
Yielding to someone’s power or authority.
Belief that events are fixed by fate and cannot be changed.

entries.sense_en: lack of feeling or interest in anything

synonyms.nuance: Not caring about a particular thing; apathy is general and lifeless.
Tired, low energy without interest.
Feeling nothing, often after shock or grief.

entries.sense_en: an ugly twist of the face showing disgust or pain

synonyms.nuance: Lowered brows, showing worry or displeasure; milder than grimace.
An angry, bad-tempered look.
A quick small movement from sudden pain or embarrassment.

entries.sense_en: harm or trouble caused by something

synonyms.nuance: General word for damage or injury.
Everyday difficulty or problem.
Wide, chaotic destruction.

entries.sense_en: badly damaged by violence, with parts of the body torn or cut

synonyms.nuance: Crushed and twisted, as in a machine or accident.
Injured so that a part of the body no longer works.
Appearance, especially the face, is spoiled.

entries.sense_en: moved his hands about to feel for something in the dark

synonyms.nuance: Search or handle something clumsily, even in daylight.
Neutral; touch to find something.
Search messily through a pile of things.

entries.sense_en: quiet and careful, so that no one notices

synonyms.nuance: Informal; sly and dishonest, often for a small trick.
Just hidden; no idea of quiet movement.
Nervous and guilty in manner, as if afraid of being caught.

entries.sense_en: in a rough, dry, low voice, here from fear

synonyms.nuance: Low and rough, sometimes attractive.
Rough and unfriendly in manner as well as voice.
Low, rough and broken like a frog’s croak, often from a cold.

entries.sense_en: a rapid, continuous series of blows or shots

synonyms.nuance: A group of shots, blows or words all at once.
Heavy, non-stop attack, including questions and criticism.
A short, sudden series.

entries.sense_en: echoed and rolled through the house

synonyms.nuance: Sound comes back after hitting a surface; the common word.
Fill a place with a loud, ringing sound.
Make a deep loud sound, without the idea of repetition.
